Install, connect a provider, then route through one endpoint

# After connecting a provider, create your OmniRoute key in Dashboard → API Keys:
curl http://localhost:20128/v1/chat/completions \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_OMNIROUTE_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"auto","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Hello!"}]}'

auto needs an eligible route. A fresh installation can have no eligible keyless targets, and a keyless provider may reject third-party clients. Providers marked tos: avoid, including Kiro, are excluded from automatic routing by default; connecting an account does not override that setting. See the Free Tiers Guide before choosing a provider.

Combos: the flagship

  1. Start with auto. Set the model in your OpenAI-compatible client. OmniRoute builds a virtual combo from connected providers and scores candidates live.
  2. Save a combo for more control. Choose a name, target list and strategy, then use that name as the model. The strategy sets which target goes first and how the rest are tried.

A combo routes across models automatically. On quota exhaustion, provider failure or model lockout, it tries the next eligible, healthy target.

Zero-config: just use auto

curl http://localhost:20128/v1/chat/completions \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <your-omniroute-key>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model": "auto", "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Hello"}]}'

Variants tune the weights. Last-known-good routing stays with the last successful provider until it fails, then rescores. auto/fast and auto/cheap express preferences without guaranteeing the fastest or cheapest model.

Model ID Behavior
auto Balanced default weights.
auto/fast Favors low latency and provider health.
auto/cheap Favors lower catalog prices.
auto/coding Quality-first weights for code generation.
auto/smart Quality-first weights with 10% exploration (default 5%).
auto/lkgp Explicit last-known-good routing with the same weights as auto.
auto/subscription Uses only live-verified plan quota. Returns HTTP 503 when none is available and avoids billed fallback.
auto/thrifty Plan → keyless → free → cheap → premium. May reach billed models and returns to the plan when quota and cooldown allow.
auto/offline Favors quota and rate-limit headroom. Requests still go to your providers.
auto/chaos One model per provider in parallel, up to five by default or ten when configured. One upstream call per model. Returns the top-ranked reply or the last successful panel reply if the top model fails. Use fusion to synthesize replies with a judge.

Category and optional tier examples include auto/coding:fast, auto/coding:free, auto/reasoning:pro and auto/vision. If no connected candidate matches, the request returns HTTP 503 and the pool stays narrow. Auto-Combo guide · Subscription-first routing

Or build your own: 22 routing strategies

omniroute combo create my-pool --strategy fill-first \
  --models "provider-a/model-1,provider-b/model-2"

The CLI accepts 15 of 22 strategies. The dashboard and combos API accept all 22.

Strategy Behavior
auto Rank candidates live with the 16-factor Auto-Combo scorer.
cache-optimized Prefer the account likely to hold the prompt prefix in cache.
context-optimized Try the largest known context window first.
context-relay Keep your order and pass a conversation summary when switching accounts.
cost-optimized Sort by catalog input-token price, unknowns last. Final request cost can differ.
expiry-first Spend quota likely to expire, highest leftover per hour until reset first.
fill-first Stay on the first available target until it runs out or fails, then move on.
fusion Query a panel in parallel and have a judge synthesize one answer.
headroom Choose the most free capacity across 5-hour and weekly windows.
jev TypeSafe Jev picks which entries in your ranked list run. Turn on COMBO_JEV_STRATEGY_ENABLED to send an excerpt per request and use paid TypeSafe calls. With it off, your order applies.
least-used Pick the target with the fewest recorded requests in this combo.
lkgp Try the last successful provider first, otherwise keep your order.
p2c Sample two targets and pick by success rate and latency.
pipeline Feed each step's output into the next target in sequence and return only the final answer.
priority Try targets in your order. Session stickiness preserves it.
quota-weighted Skip exhausted accounts and draw by leftover quota and in-flight load.
random Shuffle for each request. The same first target can repeat.
reset-aware Score remaining quota and time to reset across session and weekly windows.
reset-window Try the account whose quota window resets soonest.
round-robin Rotate in order, three successes per target by default.
strict-random Deal from a shuffled deck so each target leads once before repeats.
weighted Draw a first target by weight and keep the rest as fallbacks. The split is statistical. Use round-robin for strict rotation.

Quota strategies use live data where providers report it, including 5-hour and weekly subscription windows. fusion and pipeline make multiple upstream calls per request.

The 16-factor scorer uses quota, health, cost, latency, task fit, stability, tier priority, tier affinity, specificity match, context affinity, cache affinity, session availability, reset-window affinity, connection density, quality and reliability. Weights vary by profile. Cache affinity, reset-window affinity and reliability have zero weight by default. Scoring factors

In a saved combo with strategy: "auto", config.routerStrategy selects rules, score, cost (eco), latency (fast), sla-aware (sla), lkgp, nadir or decision. Auto router strategies

Resilience is built in: 3 independent layers

Failures are handled at three scopes, so one bad model does not take down its account, and one bad account does not take down its provider.

If a whole provider is down

The provider circuit breaker opens after 8 (OAuth) or 12 (API key) failures with status 408, 500, 502, 503 or 504. Combos skip that provider while it is open. After 60 s or 30 s, one probe request decides whether it closes.

If one key or account is rate-limited

The connection cooldown benches only that connection, with exponential backoff from 5 s (OAuth) or 3 s (API key). Other keys for the same provider keep serving.

If one model is refused

The model lockout blocks only that model on that connection after a per-model 429, 404 or access denial. Other models on the same connection keep serving.

Banned, expired and out-of-credit connections are terminal states, not cooldowns: they wait for you to fix them.

Developer notes: The project may generate a local .env file during npm install/postinstall for developer convenience. This file is intentionally ignored via .gitignore and must never be committed. If it is committed by accident, rotate any exposed secrets and remove the file from history. See docs/DEVELOPER-ENVIRONMENT.md for guidance on managing local environment files and secrets.

OmniRoute Radar

Radar is the live, signed copy of the free-tier catalog above, and it is free for everyone. There is no paywall and no waiting period. It is opt-in and GET-only. The OmniRoute client sends nothing to Radar: no prompts, traffic, provider configuration or usage telemetry.

The numbers above come from the catalog shipped with this release. Radar can show newer data between releases. New free offers and promotions are added every week. Watch the real number grow on the Radar.

OmniRoute Radar →


What's New

v3.8.54 (2026-11-17)

Latest release. Release notes.

  • Account routing. Mark Auto combo accounts Preferred, Normal, Reserve or Excluded. Enable failover to a sibling account when the preferred one is slow to respond. Auto-Combo · PR #19259
  • New combo strategies. expiry-first prioritizes quota near expiry. jev uses System One to pick a target and its fallbacks. Auto-Combo
  • Combos by endpoint. Set separate targets and strategies for chat, search and fetch, embeddings, rerank, images, video, music, OCR and audio. PR #18731
  • Agentic pipelines. Repeated tool rounds with unchanged results or consecutive failures return control to the planner. PR #19318
  • API key controls. Save reusable policies without secrets and set rolling five-hour spending limits per key. Key Templates · PR #18362
  • Provider sign-in. Use Sign in with ChatGPT for the public Responses API or sign in to Microsoft 365 Copilot with a work or school account. PR #15201 · Microsoft 365 Copilot
  • New providers. Replicate adds chat, alongside new connectors for Cerebrium, Hetzner Inference and Grokified. PR #19206

v3.8.53 (2026-11-06)

Redesigned dashboard, team cost centers, Entra ID for API access, two-factor dashboard sign-in and Kubernetes manifests. Release notes.

v3.8.52 (2026-10-19)

Headless mode, model discovery filters, per-key model pinning, the Nadir router and the LLMLingua compression sidecar. Release notes.

v3.8.51 (2026-09-30)

Subscription-first routing, the quota-weighted strategy, the orchestration dashboard, expanded language support and the OpenCode v2 plugin. Release notes.

v3.8.50 (2026-08-26)

Modality Bridge, the opt-in Radar catalog, OmniConductor fleet delegation and support for connecting the desktop app to a running server. Release notes.

See CHANGELOG.md for all changes and ROADMAP.md for planned work.


Compatible CLIs & Coding Agents

The dashboard catalog lists 39 integrations (28 coding tools and 11 agents). The CLI manifest adds Gemini CLI, which launches with omniroute run, and four tools it can only detect. Of all of them, 8 launch with omniroute run, 12 can be set up with omniroute configure, and 16 have a dedicated setup-* command. Pick the path that matches what you want.

If you want to launch a tool in one command

omniroute run starts the tool with OmniRoute's URL and key in its environment. Nothing is written to disk.

releases.body:
## OmniRoute v3.8.54

- **Providers:** official "Sign in with ChatGPT" provider (`chatgpt`, PKCE + live model discovery); MiniMax Code (managed gateway + dashboard device-code sign-in); RenderHour (images, video, speech); MegaBrain (dual auth); EmpirioLabs, ParalonCloud, deAPI, Replicate chat, Cerebrium, Hetzner Inference and Grokified; native `opencode-server` executor; Microsoft 365 Copilot work/school sign-in; GitHub Copilot embeddings; Gemini Lyria 3 music models; custom JSON API provider nodes (request template + response path).
- **Routing and combos:** endpoint-specific combo routes (chat, search/fetch, embeddings, rerank, images, video, music, OCR, audio) with capability-aware search/fetch combos; new `jev` and `expiry-first` strategies; preferred and reserve accounts for Auto combos; opt-in preferred-account response-start failover; opt-in deadline-failure sub-budget that ends a combo with a clean 504.
- **Search:** Keenable web search and fetch provider (keyless by default) and `codex-search` through connected Codex accounts.
- **API keys and usage:** `/v1/me/status` reports today's/this week's usage and every per-key limit; `/v1/me/sessions` self-service session listing;

aiSummary.oneLiner: A free AI gateway providing access to 290+ providers and 500+ models through a single endpoint.
aiSummary.whatItDoes: OmniRoute acts as a comprehensive AI gateway that unifies access to over 290 AI providers and 500+ models through a single, consistent endpoint. It is specifically designed to maximize free tier usage by aggregating the documented free limits of various providers, offering users up to ~1.53 billion free tokens per month. The gateway includes advanced routing strategies and automatic fallback mechanisms to ensure high availability and prevent rate limit errors. Furthermore, it implements RTK and Caveman stacked compression techniques to significantly reduce token usage by 15-95%. OmniRoute seamlessly integrates with popular AI coding tools like Claude Code, Cursor, and Copilot.
keyFeatures: Unified endpoint: Provides a single API endpoint to access over 500 different AI models from 290+ providers.
Free tier aggregation: Intelligently pools and tracks the free tier limits across dozens of providers to maximize cost savings.
Token compression: Utilizes RTK and Caveman compression to reduce payload sizes and save 15-95% on token consumption.
Auto-fallback routing: Automatically switches to alternative models or providers if the primary choice hits a rate limit or fails.
Tool integration: Designed to work seamlessly seamlessly with AI developer tools like Cursor, Copilot, and Claude Code.
Dashboard monitoring: Includes a comprehensive dashboard to monitor usage, track free tier budgets, and manage routing rules.

useCases.title: Cost-effective AI development
useCases.description: Developers use it to route requests through free tiers across multiple providers, drastically reducing API costs.

useCases.title: High availability AI services
useCases.description: Applications use its auto-fallback features to ensure continuous service even when specific AI providers experience downtime.

useCases.title: AI tool integration
useCases.description: Developers plug it into tools like Cursor or Cline to access premium models for free by leveraging aggregated trial credits.

useCases.title: Token optimization
useCases.description: Projects with large context windows use its compression features to fit more data into a prompt while staying within token limits.

aiSummary.whoIsItFor: OmniRoute is for developers, tinkerers, and AI tool users who want to access a wide variety of AI models without incurring high costs. It requires basic knowledge of API endpoints and configuration in developer tools.
